body_markdown:
# Daily Loop-Model Briefing - 2026-10-19

## Outcome

Five papers were added, and all of them reuse a learned block inside one forward pass. Two
study looped language-model design: a controlled comparison of loop topology, input
injection and recurrent-state design, and a causal workspace that lets positions exchange
prefix summaries between rounds. Two carry tiny recursive models to new domains, time-series
classification and spatial context prediction. The fifth uses a weight-shared recurrent
Transformer inside a query-adaptive visual tokenizer.
[RTSM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23353) cites Benhao Huang's Equilibrium Reasoners (EqR) in
its related work and appendix, where EqR's randomized-initialization and noise-injection
training motivates RTSM's depth and breadth inference probes. The Part I paper is by Benhao
Huang and coauthors; it cites EqR as related work on iterative models with random initial
states.

## Added

### Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design

[arXiv:2610.23036](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23036) · Code: [ifm-ai/xllm-loop](https://github.com/ifm-ai/xllm-loop)

**TL;DR:** Controlled from-scratch ablations separate where the loop sits, how the input is re-injected and how the recurrent state is organized; they favor the Huginn-style sandwich, which beats Ouro on all ten benchmarks at 730M parameters and keeps its lead in MoE models.

- **Setup:** dense looped LMs with 730M stored parameters (112 logical layers) trained on TxT360 for 42B–336B tokens, plus 8B-resident, 0.8B-active MoE models trained on 500B tokens. Baselines are 28-layer and 112-layer feedforward models, and a 112-layer feedforward MoE matched in training and inference FLOPs.
- **Mechanism / Method:**
  - Moves step by step from Ouro (a 28-block stack looped 4 times) to Huginn (8 prelude layers, a 12-block core looped 8 times, 8 coda layers).
  - Tests the sandwich envelope, input injection through a diagonal operator, random versus input initialization of the state, and separate high- and low-level recurrent states.
- **Results:**
  - At 336B tokens, the sandwich beats the full-stack loop on MATH500 (32.80 vs 20.80), GSM8K (62.02 vs 54.97) and BBH-CoT (48.30 vs 45.83).
  - Input injection helps knowledge retrieval and context use (MMLU +2.53, BBH-CoT +6.63) but costs some math (MATH500 −3.60).
  - Random initialization and separate H/L states give mixed or negative returns.
  - At MoE scale, Huginn beats Ouro on 8 of 10 benchmarks (GSM8K 83.62 vs 78.92) and uses 75 percent fewer resident parameters than the FLOP-matched feedforward MoE, beating it on DROP and GSM8K and matching it on MATH500.
- **Caveat:** single seed. The MoE comparison sets complete architectures against each other rather than isolating components. Extrapolation beyond the trained loop count is not tested.
- **Why added:** a controlled design study of prelude-core-coda versus whole-stack weight-tied loops, with iso-parameter, iso-depth and iso-FLOP comparisons against untied models.
- **Cites Benhao's work:** authored by Benhao Huang and coauthors. It cites Equilibrium Reasoners as related work on iterative models that use random initial states.

### Causal Latent Workspaces for Looped Transformers

[arXiv:2610.22796](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22796) · Code: [izaznov/causal-latent-workspace-transformer](https://github.com/izaznov/causal-latent-workspace-transformer)

**TL;DR:** Between rounds of a shared Transformer block, each position writes gated vectors into prefix-specific latent slots and reads a content-addressed summary back; this gives the best mean perplexity in five of six byte-level settings.

- **Setup:** byte-level language modeling on WikiText-103 raw, enwik8 and TinyStories at two parameter budgets (0.918M and 101.71M), three seeds each. Controls are a plain untied 4-layer Transformer, shared loops with and without input anchoring, an adaptive-exit mixture and a conditioned dense model, all with parameter counts matched and four block applications.
- **Mechanism / Method:** one causal Transformer block is applied for four rounds. The original embedding is re-injected every round, and a causal workspace built from causal cumulative sums gives each position a summary of its prefix before the next application.
- **Results:**
  - At 101.71M parameters, perplexity is 2.7820, 2.7843 and 1.6823 on the three corpora, improving on the strongest non-workspace control by 1.06, 0.73 and 1.01 percent. All nine seed-level comparisons favor the workspace.
  - Every shared loop beats the untied plain Transformer at matched parameters; the workspace model is 6.71–8.19 percent lower in perplexity at the larger budget.
  - At 0.918M parameters, a conditioned loop is still better on enwik8.
- **Caveat:** small training budgets (81.92M training targets), byte-level text only, and FLOPs are not matched. The gains over the best control are about 1 percent.
- **Why added:** adds a new loop-time state path to a fully weight-tied looped Transformer.

### RTSM: Adapting Recursive Models to Multivariate Time-Series Classification

[arXiv:2610.23353](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23353) · Code: none stated

**TL;DR:** A convolutional tokenizer feeds a single-state, weight-tied refinement module in the style of tiny recursive models, and the classifier averages 72.81 percent accuracy over all 30 UEA datasets, the best of 17 deep models.

- **Setup:** one model per UEA multivariate dataset, compared with 16 deep baselines from the MambaSL benchmark. Ablations use eight datasets and three seeds.
- **Mechanism / Method:** a two-block attention and SwiGLU module updates one latent state as z ← f(z + x). Training uses TRM-style deep supervision with correctness-based halting; inference runs 16 supervision steps of three cycles, i.e. 48 applications of the same 6.82M-parameter module.
- **Results:**
  - 72.81 percent mean accuracy with validation-based selection, 1.60 points above MambaSL; top five on 21 of 30 datasets.
  - The full classifier reaches 86.10 percent against 84.79 for a tokenizer-only classifier on the ablation datasets, and the single-state design beats two-state variants (84.98 and 84.29).
  - Untied weights for the same 48 applications would need 327.16M parameters.
- **Caveat:** extra inference depth helps only slightly (72.42 at one step, 72.84 at 64). The ablations do not hold parameters or compute fixed.
- **Why added:** weight-tied recursive refinement within one forward pass, applied to time-series classification.
- **Cites Benhao's work:** yes. It cites Equilibrium Reasoners (Huang, Geng, Kolter) in related work and in its appendix, as the source of randomized-initialization and noise-injection training for depth and breadth scaling, which it lists as untested follow-up work.

### Look, Reason, Draw a Region: Recursive Refinement for Spatial Context Prediction

[arXiv:2610.23302](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23302) · Code: none stated

**TL;DR:** Spatial-TRM runs a two-state tiny recursive reasoner over frozen DINOv3 vision-language features and decodes a convex region; it improves RoboSpatial-Home context accuracy from 20.49 to 29.51 percent over a single-step model with the same parameters.

- **Setup:** 40,000 RoboSpatial training samples; evaluation on the 122 RoboSpatial-Home context questions. The model has 11.2M trainable parameters (877.8M with frozen encoders).
- **Mechanism / Method:** a cross-attention grounding step feeds a TRM-style core in which reasoning and answer states are both updated by the same two-layer Transformer, with deep recursion and deep supervision. A convex half-plane decoder turns the answer state into a region.
- **Results:**
  - 29.51 percent context accuracy, against 20.49 for a separately trained single-step model at equal parameters and 17.21 for a feedforward variant.
  - RoboPoint-13B scores 31.10 and RoboRefer-8B 61.48.
  - Cutting latent recursion to one step at inference drops accuracy to 14.75.
- **Caveat:** a 122-question test set, where one question is worth about 0.8 points. Baselines are reported scores, not re-runs, and the recursive model uses more compute than the single-step one.
- **Why added:** a hierarchical weight-tied recursive core applied to visual spatial reasoning.

### Query-adaptive Recurrent Tokenization

[arXiv:2610.22957](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22957) · Code: none (the paper says it cannot be released)

**TL;DR:** QART builds query-conditioned visual tokens with a weight-shared recurrent Transformer, adds slots until query-relevant features are reconstructed well enough, then halts; it keeps 93.8 percent of dense VQAv2 accuracy with about 25x fewer tokens.

- **Setup:** frozen SigLIP2-style vision and text encoders, a cross-modal relevance module, the recurrent slot tokenizer and a downstream VLM or task head. Evaluated on Visual7W, VQAv2, CORE and PODS.
- **Mechanism / Method:** a three-layer Transformer is shared across recurrent rounds, with a learned round embedding added to active slots. After each round a shared decoder reconstructs the query-relevant features; low coverage adds slots, and recurrence halts once coverage passes a threshold (between two and six rounds).
- **Results:**
  - 81.96 percent on Visual7W and 76.37 percent on VQAv2 with about 29 visual tokens, 20–25x fewer than dense inputs.
  - 92.0 percent P@1 on CORE and 36.3 percent PR-AUC on PODS, 8.4 percent above SteerViT.
  - 1.53x end-to-end throughput at batch size 8.
- **Caveat:** the loop serves token-budget adaptation rather than reasoning depth, and the throughput gain is reported at batch size 8 only.
- **Why added:** a weight-shared recurrent block with input-dependent halting inside the tokenizer's single forward pass.

## Catalog update

- Added official code links, each stated in the paper's own arXiv full text, to five papers:
  [Positive concave deep equilibrium models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04029),
  [Dense Supervision Is Not Enough](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24898),
  [Think Deep, Speak Once: ReLIT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08113),
  [Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11233)
  and [LoopSpec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184).
- No venue changed. No new official acceptance records were found for this group of papers.

## Near misses

- [ReLaDrift](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23225) refines a draft by calling the whole Drifting
  generator again each round, which is iterative generation rather than a reused internal block.
- [BRICE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23001) iterates a predictive-coding encoder for a few
  steps, but the paper never states that weights are shared across those steps.
- [Sep-Latent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22924) compresses chain-of-thought into latent
  separator tokens decoded autoregressively by the full model.
- [Really Need Recursion?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22423) replaces recursive registration
  with a one-pass network; no block is reused.
